items.title: Driver Remained at Scene After Child Struck on Hillcrest Avenue in Cooksville, Police Say
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a child was struck by a vehicle Monday afternoon in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood. According to police, the incident happened on Hillcrest Avenue near Confederation Parkway, just north of Dundas Street East. CTV News reports the driver remained at the scene after the collision. Police told the outlet the child was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. According to police, the investigation is ongoing, and anyone with further information is asked to contact Peel police or Crime Stoppers.

items.title: Peel Public Health Opens Respiratory Vaccine Clinics in Mississauga Starting This Week
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Public Health is opening vaccination clinics this week as officials urge residents to protect themselves against flu, COVID-19 and RSV ahead of the colder months. According to the outlet, appointments for high-risk and priority groups begin Wednesday, Oct. 21, with vaccines opening to the general population aged six months and older on Monday, Oct. 26. The outlet reports both clinics are located at 7120 Hurontario St. in Mississauga, serving residents of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. Peel's Medical Officer of Health, Dr. Alexa Caturay, said vaccination is an important way for residents to protect themselves and their families as people spend more time indoors and respiratory viruses spread more easily. According to Insauga.com, health officials say the shots do not eliminate the chance of infection but can lower the risk of serious illness, particularly for older adults, young children and pregnant people.

items.title: Streetsville's Final Fall Walking Tour Retraces the Night a Crowd Silenced Solomon Northup in 1857
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the final Streetsville Historic Walking Tour of the 2026 season, set for Wednesday, Oct. 21, will focus on Solomon Northup, whose memoir Twelve Years a Slave inspired the Oscar-winning 2013 film of the same name. According to the outlet, the tour will revisit Northup's visit to Streetsville in August 1857, when a hostile crowd prevented him from speaking about his experiences at what is now Streetsville Village Square. The outlet reports the tour is led by local historian Richard Collins, who guided the village's walking tours throughout the year. Insauga.com says Northup was born a free man in New York around 1807, kidnapped and sold into slavery in 1841, and endured 12 years of enslavement in Louisiana before regaining his freedom in 1853 and publishing his memoir. According to the outlet, Northup travelled to Canada four years later to lecture about slavery with support from the Anti-Slavery Society of Canada, a trip that brought him to Streetsville.

items.title: 127 Kilograms of Cocaine Seized at Ambassador Bridge Leads to Charges Against Two Mississauga Men
items.summary: Insauga.com reports two Mississauga men face drug charges after Canada Border Services Agency officers discovered a large stash of cocaine inside a commercial truck trying to enter the country from the United States. According to the outlet, CBSA officers and a drug detector dog found 127 kilograms of suspected cocaine hidden inside the trailer at the Ambassador Bridge in Windsor after the vehicle was flagged for a secondary examination. The outlet reports CBSA officers seized the drugs, arrested the two men, and turned both the cocaine and the suspects over to the RCMP. Insauga.com says RCMP Central Region border integrity operations officer Tim Diebel credited the seizure to the close cooperation between the RCMP, CBSA and other law enforcement agencies working to keep illicit drugs out of Canada. According to the outlet, officials said the officers' attention to detail and use of technology helped stop a significant amount of cocaine from reaching Canadian communities.

items.title: Entrepreneurs Can Compete for $30,000 as Startup Canada Tour Makes Its Final 2026 Stop in Mississauga
items.summary: The City of Mississauga reports the city will host the final stop of the 2026 Startup Canada Tour at the Living Arts Centre on Oct. 29, one of only three Canadian cities selected this year. According to the city, the event will bring together entrepreneurs, investors, mentors and business leaders from across the country, building on the success of last year's stop. The city says the tour is presented by Pizza Hut, Scotiabank and UPS, with IDEA Mississauga and Visit Mississauga supporting as local partners. According to the city, entrepreneurs can compete in the Startup Global National Pitch Competition for a chance to win $8,500 and a spot in the Grand Finale in Mississauga, where finalists vie for a $30,000 national prize. The city reports attendees will also vote for a $1,000 People's Choice Award winner and can catch a fireside chat featuring Donna Heslin and Gharsa Amin.

items.title: Mississauga Schools Have Until Oct. 31 to Sign Up for Spring's Car-Free Drop-Off Pilot
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga is inviting more local schools to join a national School Streets pilot that temporarily closes roads to vehicle traffic during school drop-off and pickup times. According to the outlet, the program targets early morning and mid-afternoon periods when large numbers of students are entering or leaving the building, reducing congestion and making it easier for kids to walk, bike or roll to school. The city says it first joined the nationwide initiative in 2022 and is now reintroducing it for a spring 2027 pilot, with public and Catholic elementary and middle schools able to sign up until Oct. 31. Insauga.com reports two Mississauga schools, Sts. Peter and Paul Catholic Elementary and Corliss Public School in Malton, took part last year. The outlet says Sts. Peter and Paul, near Rathburn Road East and Central Parkway East, blocked front-of-building vehicle access at specific times for nearly four weeks during its spring participation, in a direct attempt to improve road safety around the school.

items.title: From Port Credit Farmers' Market to a Permanent Storefront: Butter Bar Boutique Expands Into Wholesale
items.summary: Retail Insider reports Mississauga entrepreneur Kate Engineer has opened her flavoured-butter company's first permanent storefront while expanding into wholesale distribution with other Ontario food businesses. According to the outlet, Butter Bar Boutique is located at 1006 Lagoon St. in the Port Credit area and sells the company's gourmet flavoured butters alongside specialty foods, kitchen products and gifts emphasizing locally made Canadian goods. The outlet reports Engineer founded Butter Bar in 2023 and spent its first three years personally churning, flavouring, packaging and selling every stick before partnering with family-owned The Alliston Creamery to scale up production. Retail Insider says the company now also supplies its packaged butters to other retailers, including SanRemo Bakery and Downey's Farm Market, with products on shelves there over the recent Thanksgiving weekend. Engineer told the outlet she started Butter Bar out of a love for butter and cooking, crediting the Port Credit Farmers' Market and pop-up shops like the One of a Kind Show for helping the business grow.

items.title: Mississauga Council Approves Plan to Cut Road Salt Use and Expand Winter Parking Bans
items.summary: Modern Mississauga Media reports Mississauga City Council has approved changes to winter road maintenance aimed at making snow clearing more efficient and environmentally friendly. According to the outlet, the city will launch a Low Road Salt Strategy this winter while also expanding winter parking restrictions to include 15-hour no-parking areas. The outlet reports the new strategy builds on the city's existing Salt Management Plan, which already pre-treats roads with brine, plows more frequently and uses weather-watch technology. According to Modern Mississauga, the city plans to use anti-icing brine on 20 per cent more roads, a move it says could save up to 650 tonnes of salt each winter, and to plow select major roads earlier so less salt is needed, saving up to 3,450 tonnes. The outlet says the city will also test magnesium-treated road salt on select sidewalks and bus stops, which officials believe works longer and may reduce how often it needs to be reapplied.

items.title: 128 Charges Laid in Mississauga as Peel Police Dismantle Carjacking Ring Across the GTA
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Peel police arrested 10 men and laid more than 120 charges following an eight-month investigation into a series of violent carjackings and luxury vehicle thefts across the Toronto area. According to police, the probe, dubbed Project High Guard, examined 21 incidents between June 2025 and April 2026 in which suspects allegedly used knives and firearms to threaten victims, some of whom were hospitalized with severe injuries. The outlet reports investigators uncovered what they describe as a criminal network responsible for planning robberies, targeting specific vehicles, recruiting younger offenders and arranging the sale of stolen cars. Det. Sgt. Earl Scott of Peel police's central robbery bureau said at a news conference at force headquarters in Mississauga that investigators were able to identify multiple levels of the alleged organization. According to the Star, coordinated search warrants executed Sept. 3 across Peel Region, Halton Region and Toronto led to the 10 arrests and the eventual 128 charges.

items.title: Brampton Councillor Says She Was Told She 'Deserved to Be Raped and Killed' as Female Politicians Describe Harassment Ahead of Oct. 26 Vote
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports that female politicians across Peel and Halton say gender-based harassment and intimidation are far from rare for women in municipal politics, with many describing their experiences ahead of the Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, Brampton councillor Rowena Santos said she has faced sexist treatment and serious threats to her physical safety during her time on council. Santos, one of two female councillors in Brampton and the first Filipino person elected to the council, told the outlet two people threatened her, telling her she deserved to be raped and killed. The outlet reports her ethnicity has also drawn targeted criticism. Mississauga.com says the accounts echo similar experiences shared by other female politicians contacted in Peel and Halton, many of whom are seeking re-election this cycle, suggesting the hostility Santos described is not an isolated incident.
